hypotheses.justification: This instance can be recovered from `hvol`: positivity of `(volume U).toReal` implies `volume U < ⊤` (by `ENNReal.toReal_pos_iff`), and the restricted measure has total mass `volume U`. Thus the proof can install the finite-measure instance locally. This also handles the zero-volume case, which `hvol` excludes.

With the finite-measure instance obtained from `hvol`, the constant function `u x` is integrable on `U`. The pointwise segment estimate `norm_sub_le_integral_norm_fderiv_mul_norm_sub_along_segment huDiff x y` bounds `‖u x - u y‖` by the integrable function supplied by `hsegment`. Since `huDiff` makes `u` continuous and hence strongly measurable, domination gives integrability of `u x - u y`, and subtracting it from the integrable constant function gives `IntegrableOn u U`. That derived integrability supplies the hypothesis needed by the existing average estimate; no degenerate case is lost.
